column2: the wolf-spirit of Ulric
the bear-rage of Ursun
the fury of Grimnir
the howling rage of the northern gods

As the enemy line draws near, something wakes in you that you have never felt before: [Root.GetBerserkerSpirit]. Your blood roars in your ears, you bite down on the rim of your shield until the wood splinters, and with a howl that is not your own you hurl yourself alone into the enemy ranks. The cowards break and run at the sight of you, and your axe has no mercy for them.
Must... kill... more...

Shaking with the rage, you cleave the skull of yet another foe and turn to look for the next. Only then do you notice that your leg will not carry you: a spear has gone clean through it, and the bone beneath is shattered.
Only a flesh wound...
Shaking with the rage, you cleave the skull of yet another foe and turn to look for the next. Only then do you notice the long arrow standing out of your thigh, and the blood running into your boot.
Only a flesh wound...

The rage has carried you deep into the enemy ranks, and your own warriors are far behind. An arrow bites into your shoulder and two more into your chest. You throw your shield aside, take your axe in both hands and split one more skull before you fall to your knees. Then they are on you like a pack of dogs.
It is a good day to die...

Your sight turns red and [Root.GetBerserkerSpirit] takes you. You charge without a thought for your own skin, and while your companions struggle to keep up, your axe cuts a wide swath through the enemy. When the dust settles they find you standing over a heap of the slain, still snarling.
*a long, guttural howl*

You have been cheated of a glorious death in battle, and now the years have caught up with you. When the rage comes, your heart pounds until you cannot breathe, and your arms are heavy before the fight has well begun. The rage is for the young.
Perhaps it is.

[berserk_courtier.GetTitledFirstName] has been droning on at you for an hour about some trifle or other, and the rage is rising. You bite down hard on the edge of the table and taste blood and splinters. Froth gathers at the corners of your mouth, and your sight is starting to turn red...
Gggh... m-must... control... r-rage...
You may lose control.
You may hold the rage back.

When your servants burst in to see what the noise is, [berserk_courtier.GetTitledFirstName] stumbles past them with torn clothes, a mouth short of several teeth and a face swelling purple, and runs as if a bear were after [berserk_courtier.GetHerHim]. You sit among the wreckage, panting, waiting for the red to leave your eyes.
I probably should not have done that...

You bite a great chunk out of the table and spit it out while [berserk_courtier.GetTitledFirstName] goes on and on. With every scrap of your will you turn the rage away from [berserk_courtier.GetHerHim] and onto the table, and you hew it into firewood with your axe. As you lie panting in the splinters, [berserk_courtier.GetFirstName] finally stops to ask if you are feeling well, my [Root.GetTitle].
Yes... yes. I just need a moment.
the Blood God's fury

As the enemy draws near, you feel Khorne's gaze fall upon you. A blood-lust you cannot master swells in your chest, red-hot, and with a howl you raise your weapon and charge alone into the enemy ranks. Many of the cowards flee at the mere sight of you, but your axe has no mercy to spare for them. Blood for the Blood God!
Blood! Hahahahaha... BLOOD!

Touched by the Blood God's gift of madness, you cleave the skull of yet another fool who dared stand before you. Another corpse for the pile. Only as you turn to seek more blood do you notice that your leg will no longer carry you: a spear has gone clean through it.
I will have the last blood!

Touched by the Blood God's gift of madness, you split in twain yet another foe who thought to match your might. Another skull for the Throne. Only as you turn to seek more blood do you notice the axe stuck in your back.
Is that all?

Your sight turns red as the rage takes you completely, and you find yourself charging the enemy lines alone. As you swing at the nearest foe, an arrow burrows into your shoulder and two more into your chest. Spitting blood, you wield your fury like another weapon and cut down one more before they surround you and hurl themselves at you like a pack of rabid dogs.
So much blood... too much to drink.

The rage overwhelms you. Howling and snarling like a madman, you charge ahead without a thought for your own skin, and while your companions struggle to keep up you give yourself to Khorne and drown in the blood and carnage of the press. When the dust settles, your retainers find you standing over a few dozen slain, sawing at a neck for one more skull.
Uuuaaarrarraaargh!

[berserk_courtier.GetTitledFirstName] drones on as the rage of Khorne builds in you, but with a great effort you turn it away from [berserk_courtier.GetHerHim]. Your blade bites instead into a servant who had the bad luck to be passing with a jug, and the rage slowly ebbs. [berserk_courtier.GetFirstName] holds [berserk_courtier.GetHerHis] breath and chooses the next words very carefully, my [Root.GetTitle]. Khorne cares not from whence the blood flows, but he saw you hold back, and he is not pleased.
I will kill you next time.
